inputs.original_text: John Lahart is right that people without children shouldn’t be treated as less deserving under inheritance tax rules. But fairness can’t stop at recognizing different family structures: inheritance itself lets wealth and advantage pass down, reinforcing inequality. Reform should protect people from discrimination without giving those with wealth more ways to preserve privilege, and ensure public resources aren’t sacrificed to private inheritance.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right that people without children shouldn’t be treated as less deserving under inheritance tax rules. But equal treatment across family structures is only part of the picture: inheritance allows wealth and advantage to accumulate across generations, while everyone else is left to contend with unequal opportunities. Reform should protect people from discrimination without expanding the ability of the wealthy to preserve privilege, and it must not put private inheritance ahead of the public resources we all rely on.
